items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: His great favorites were Caruso and John McCormack.

ctx.x: Yeah. That’s a good all-purpose term. And you were saying something yesterday I thought was really fascinating about how instrumentalists copied vocalists and how vocalists copied instrumentalists. And you had this kind of round about pattern.

Absolutely. Well Armstrong is a great illustration because he sings the way he plays the trumpet, and he plays as a trumpet player like a singer. And you know he always stressed that he got his lyrical style of playing trumpet by listening to operatic arias. His great favorites were Caruso and John McCormack. And if you make comparisons, it’s easy to see that the lyric quality of these great operatic tenors is absolutely part and parcel Armstrong style. He’s the great lyric interpreter on an instrument, just as…
the early part of the century who made the earliest records have preserved the history of singing up to that point.
